descriptionChirho: Ground grain flour or meal (קֶמַח), the common cereal product used in food preparation throughout the OT, whether for baking bread (1Sa 28:24; 2Sa 17:28; 1Ki 5:2; 17:12,14,16; 2Ki 4:41; Isa 47:2; Hos 8:7), in offerings (Nu 5:15; Jdg 6:19), or as part of hospitality provisions (Gen 18:6; 1Sa 1:24). All three clusters are grammatical variants: absolute/construct, with article, and with conjunction waw. Arabic uniformly renders 'دَقِيق,' Korean '가루/밀가루,' Swahili 'unga,' Spanish 'harina,' and Hindi 'आटा,' confirming a single undifferentiated sense of milled grain.
